authoredPrompt: This figure is a four-column visualization of the activations inside a small neural network, the columns arranged left to right as successive stages of training. Each column is a vertical stack of seven flat square planes in isometric perspective, one plane per layer output, joined by dashed trajectory curves that carry every datapoint from one plane to the next. Points appear in two colors, red and blue. In all four columns the bottom plane shows the two colors thoroughly intermingled in a dense central cluster, and moving upward they are pulled apart, the red trajectories drawing into a tight vertical bundle while the blue ones bow outward to one side. A legend column at the far left gives the architecture as a bottom-to-top chain of arrows and rounded labels reading linear, relu, linear, relu, linear, and softmax. Beneath the panels a long horizontal arrow labeled Training iteration runs the full width, with sets of three dots between columns marking skipped iterations. Reading up a column shows how one forward pass reshapes the data distribution layer by layer; reading across shows the separation growing cleaner and the blue points swinging farther out as training proceeds.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for training iteration; the learner scrubs left to right through training, the red and blue trajectories update from mixed to separated, and the relationship between optimization progress and class separability becomes clear.
- Button/state for layer-by-layer forward pass; the learner steps upward through linear, relu, linear, relu, linear, and softmax planes, the active plane and incoming trajectories highlight, and it becomes clear how each layer reshapes the same points.
- Hover over one datapoint trajectory; the learner traces a single red or blue point through all planes, its path brightens across the stack, and the continuity between layerwise transformations and the final class bundle becomes clear.

discrepancies: The red and blue trajectory bundles are much sparser and less dense than in the source, especially the large blue fan-out in later training snapshots.
The grey dashed bounding/corner guide lines between planes are mostly absent, making the layered 3D transformation cages less faithful.
The stacks are compressed and visually small relative to the canvas compared with the source, reducing the prominence of the layered structures.
The later training columns do not reproduce the strong wide deformation and outward sweeping trajectories shown in the source; the generated paths remain comparatively narrow and orderly.
The source emphasizes four large snapshot columns with dense overlaid activations, while the generated figure appears simplified with fewer datapoints and cleaner, less chaotic geometry.
evaluation.notes: The figure is recognizable as stacked neural activations over training with correct labels and useful interactions, but it is simplified, under-dense, and missing many grey guide structures and dramatic trajectory deformations from the source.
action_items: Increase the number and density of red and blue datapoint trajectories to better match the crowded source figure.
Add the grey dashed corner-to-corner guide cages between successive planes in each stack.
Scale up the main figure and reduce empty canvas space so the four snapshot stacks dominate the composition as in the source.
Make later training snapshots show much wider blue fan-out and stronger red/blue geometric deformation.

feedback.rationale: The concept, labels, and interactions are strong, but the critic identifies implementation-level visual issues—density, guide cages, scaling, and deformation strength—that the generator can refine without changing the plan.
